label: <DEL> step of long sequences whose first token is s/t/j/y/r/g/3/p/v/i
explanation: Fires almost never in the original phase. 67% of activation mass falls on the <DEL> step (recall_idx 0), but only 8% of <DEL> steps fire. The rest is on early copy steps (recall_idx 1-3), plus a little near the end. Firing rate and magnitude go up with sequence length (L=9 holds 47% of mass) and depend on the token about to be output: s, t, j, y are strongest (rate 6-9%), then r, g, 3, p, v, i. The largest activations are on <DEL> when orig(0) is s/t/j, often with a smaller echo on the next step or two. It is weak or silent when the token being output is a letter outside that set. The predicate covers about 52% of mass at about 32% precision on dev. Many sequences that satisfy it do not fire, and the extra dependence on other prefix tokens could not be captured simply.
